card.name: Words just before a dash or comma
card.fires_on: General web prose, on a word that ends a phrase or clause just before a dash, colon or comma. Examples are "climate change" before an em dash and "growth factor" before a comma.

modes.label: Before an em dash
modes.description: A phrase-ending noun right before a dash that opens an aside.
modes.example: the greenhouse gas most responsible for climate<< change>> — and transformed it back

modes.label: Mid-clause words
modes.description: An ordinary word inside a clause, such as a verb, adverb or noun, where the sentence goes on.
modes.example: it burns<< more>> cleanly than petroleum

modes.label: Before a colon or list
modes.description: A word that introduces a following item, quotation or list.

card.plain: It fires on ordinary words in web articles where the next mark is unlikely to be a dash, and it discourages dashes.
